plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. This holds regardless of other bidders' beliefs about my strategy, since my payment doesn't depend on my own bid amount when I win. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, since your payment doesn't depend on your own bid (only on whether you win). Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $27 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it doesn't matter what others bid or think about my strategy. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below, I risk losing an item I'd profit from. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' rationality or beliefs, my optimal action is to bid exactly my true value of $13.
